misconception.zh: 虚数是不存在的数，是硬编出来凑答案的。
misconception.en: Imaginary numbers don't really exist; they were made up to force an answer.

insight.zh: 乘负一是让箭头绕零转半圈；如果乘法也要能表示转九十度，那个数乘两次就是转半圈，也就是乘负一，所以它的平方必须是负一，这就是 i。i 不在数轴上，数轴要扩成一个平面，乘 i 就是整个平面转九十度。
insight.en: Times negative one turns an arrow half a turn around zero. If multiplication is also to turn by ninety degrees, doing that number twice is a half turn, which is times negative one, so its square must be negative one: that is i. i is not on the number line, so the line grows into a plane, and multiplying by i turns the whole plane by ninety degrees.

non_example.zh: 乘 i 不是加 i：三加 i 再加 i 是往上挪一格，到三加二 i，箭头没有转；三加 i 乘 i 才转到负一加三 i。
non_example.en: Times i is not plus i: 3 + i plus i just moves up one square to 3 + 2i, and the arrow doesn't turn; 3 + i times i turns to −1 + 3i.

stem.zh: 数轴上有没有一个数，平方以后是负数？
stem.en: Is there a number on the number line whose square is negative?

zh: 没有：正数和负数的平方都是正的
en: No: positive and negative numbers both square to positive

stem.zh: 为什么 i×i 必须等于 −1？
stem.en: Why must i×i equal −1?

zh: 乘 i 转 90°，两次就是转 180°，而转 180° 就是乘 −1
这是人为规定的，没有理由
en: Times i turns 90°, twice is 180°, and a 180° turn is times −1
It's an arbitrary rule with no reason

stem.zh: 乘 i 和加 i 有什么不同？
stem.en: How is multiplying by i different from adding i?

zh: 乘 i 绕原点转 90°，加 i 往上平移一格
乘 i 把箭头拉长
en: They're the same: both go up
Times i turns 90° about 0; plus i shifts up one square
Times i makes the arrow longer

stem.zh: 1 连乘 i 四次，依次落在哪？
stem.en: Multiply 1 by i four times. Where does it land each time?
Example: (3+i)×i = −1+3i. What is (2+5i)×i?

stem.zh: i³ 等于多少？
stem.en: What is i³?

stem.zh: (4−i)×i 等于多少？
stem.en: What is (4−i)×i?

stem.zh: i⁴ 等于多少？
stem.en: What is i⁴?

stem.zh: 点 (2,1) 绕原点逆时针转 90° 到哪？
stem.en: Where does the point (2,1) go when turned 90° counterclockwise about the origin?

stem.zh: z 乘 −i 是怎么转？
stem.en: How does multiplying z by −i turn it?

next_hook.zh: 能不能把整个平面拉一拉、扭一扭，也写成乘法？
next_hook.en: Could stretching and twisting the whole plane be written as a multiplication too?

transcript.zh: 四百多年前，数学家解三次方程，算到一半冒出了负数开平方。
transcript.en: Over four hundred years ago, mathematicians solving cubic equations hit the square root of a negative number halfway through.

transcript.zh: 一个平方等于负一的数，你觉得能有吗？
transcript.en: A number whose square is negative one: do you think it can exist?

transcript.zh: 当时不少人直摇头：这种数根本不存在，是硬编出来凑答案的。
transcript.en: Plenty of people back then shook their heads: such numbers don't exist, they were just made up to force an answer.

transcript.zh: 我们一起看。还记得负负得正吗？乘负一就是转半圈。
transcript.en: Let's look together. Remember negative times negative? Times negative one is a half turn.

transcript.zh: 三乘负一，就是让箭头绕零转半圈，从三转到负三。
transcript.en: Three times negative one: the arrow turns half a turn around zero, from three to negative three.

transcript.zh: 转半圈是乘负一，那转四分之一圈，是乘什么？
transcript.en: Half a turn is times negative one. What would a quarter turn be?

transcript.zh: 假设有一个数，乘它一次，箭头就转九十度。
transcript.en: Suppose there is a number that turns things ninety degrees when you multiply by it.

transcript.zh: 一乘它，箭头转到正上方；再乘它，就转到了负一。
transcript.en: One times it: the arrow turns straight up. Times it again: it turns to negative one.

transcript.zh: 乘它两次就是转了半圈，也就是乘了负一。
transcript.en: Twice is a half turn, which is times negative one.

transcript.zh: 所以这个数的平方必须是负一，我们叫它 i。
transcript.en: So this number's square has to be negative one. We call it i.

transcript.zh: 数轴上找不到它，它在零的正上方，数轴要扩成平面。
transcript.en: It isn't on the number line: it sits straight above zero, so the line has to grow into a plane.

transcript.zh: 我们来验证一下：三加 i 乘 i，按分配律展开算。
transcript.en: Let's check: three plus i, times i, using the distributive law.

transcript.zh: 结果是三 i 加 i 的平方，也就是负一加三 i。
transcript.en: We get three i plus i squared, which is negative one plus three i.

transcript.zh: 放到平面上看，乘 i 就是让整个平面绕着零转九十度。
transcript.en: On the plane, times i turns the whole plane by ninety degrees.

transcript.zh: 三加 i 正好转到负一加三 i，算的和转的一样。
transcript.en: Three plus i lands exactly on negative one plus three i: the algebra and the turn agree.

transcript.zh: 注意，乘 i 可不是加 i，这两件事很容易混。
transcript.en: Careful: times i is not plus i.

transcript.zh: 三加 i 再加 i，只是往上挪一格，到三加二 i，没有转。
transcript.en: Three plus i, plus i, just moves up one square to three plus two i. No turn.

transcript.zh: 所以 i 乘 i 等于负一：转两次九十度，就是转半圈。
transcript.en: So i times i is negative one: two ninety-degree turns make a half turn.

transcript.zh: 负负得正是转两次半圈，正好转回原来的方向。
transcript.en: Negative times negative is two half turns, back to where it started.

transcript.zh: 虚数不是硬编出来的，它是让乘法能够转弯的那个数。
transcript.en: Imaginary numbers aren't made up. They are the numbers that let multiplication turn.

transcript.zh: 能不能把整个平面拉一拉、扭一扭，也写成乘法？
transcript.en: Could stretching and twisting the whole plane be written as a multiplication too?

title.zh: 矩阵是把整个平面变形
title.en: A Matrix Transforms the Whole Plane

aha.zh: 2×2 矩阵到底"做"了什么？

misconception.zh: 矩阵只是四个数排成的一张表，跟拉、转、推没什么关系。
misconception.en: A matrix is just four numbers in a table, with nothing to do with stretching, turning or pushing.

insight.zh: 二乘二的矩阵把整个平面像橡皮膜一样一起变形；平面上画一座小房子，地板方向和墙的方向各放一支箭头，矩阵的第一列写着地板箭头去了哪，第二列写着墙箭头去了哪。放大、横拉、转九十度、推斜，每一个动作都只是这两支箭头换了地方。
insight.en: A 2×2 matrix deforms the whole plane at once, like a rubber sheet. Draw a little house with one arrow along the floor and one up the wall: the first column says where the floor arrow goes, the second where the wall arrow goes. Scaling, stretching, turning and shearing are all just those two arrows moving.

non_example.zh: 把同样四个数按行来读：地板去 (2,1)、墙去 (0,1)，房子歪到另一边，和按列读的样子完全不同。
non_example.en: Read the same four numbers by rows: the floor goes to (2,1) and the wall to (0,1), and the house leans the other way, nothing like reading by columns.

stem.zh: 矩阵 (3 0; 0 3) 会把一座小房子变成什么样？
stem.en: What does the matrix (3 0; 0 3) do to a little house?

stem.zh: 为什么只要知道地板箭头和墙箭头去哪，就知道整座房子去哪？
stem.en: Why does knowing where the floor and wall arrows go tell you where the whole house goes?

zh: 房子上每个点都是几个地板箭头加几个墙箭头，变形后照样这么拼
en: Every point of the house is some floor arrows plus some wall arrows, built the same way after the change
Because the house has only five corners
Because a matrix has only four numbers

stem.zh: 先转 90° 再横拉 2 倍，和先横拉再转，地板箭头落在同一个地方吗？
stem.en: Turn 90° then stretch sideways by 2, or stretch then turn: does the floor arrow land in the same place?

en: No: one lands at (0,1), the other at (0,2)

stem.zh: 推斜矩阵 (1 1; 0 1) 把单位方格变成平行四边形，面积变成多少？
stem.en: The shear (1 1; 0 1) turns the unit square into a parallelogram. What is its area?

stem.zh: 看例子：(2 1; 0 1) 把地板箭头送到 (2,0)、墙箭头送到 (1,1)。(3 1; 1 2) 把它们送到哪？
stem.en: Example: (2 1; 0 1) sends the floor arrow to (2,0) and the wall arrow to (1,1). Where does (3 1; 1 2) send them?

stem.zh: 把地板箭头送到 (1,2)、墙箭头送到 (−1,0) 的矩阵是什么？
stem.en: Which matrix sends the floor arrow to (1,2) and the wall arrow to (−1,0)?

stem.zh: 矩阵 (3 1; 1 2) 的行列式（面积放大倍数）是多少？
stem.en: What is the determinant (area scale factor) of (3 1; 1 2)?
Where does (0 −1; 1 0) send the point (3,1)?

stem.zh: (2 4; 1 2) 的两列在同一条直线上。它把房子压成什么？
stem.en: The columns of (2 4; 1 2) lie on one line. What does it squash the house into?

next_hook.zh: 要是两支箭头被压到同一条线上，房子会变成什么？
next_hook.en: If the two arrows got squashed onto one line, what would become of the house?

transcript.zh: 在修图软件里拉宽、转动、推歪一张图，程序只记下四个数。
transcript.en: In a photo editor, when you stretch a picture, turn it or push it sideways, the program only records four numbers.

transcript.zh: 这四个数到底在做什么？先在心里想一想。
transcript.en: What are those four numbers actually doing? Think about it first.

transcript.zh: 看上去它们只是排成一张表，跟拉、转、推好像没什么关系。
transcript.en: They look like just a table of numbers, with nothing to do with stretching, turning or pushing.

transcript.zh: 我们一起看。把平面想成一张橡皮膜，上面画一座小房子。
transcript.en: Let's look together. Think of the plane as a rubber sheet with a little house drawn on it.

transcript.zh: 地板方向放一支箭头，墙的方向也放一支箭头。
transcript.en: Put one arrow along the floor and one up the wall.

transcript.zh: 先把整张膜放大两倍：地板箭头到了二、零，墙的到了零、二。
transcript.en: First blow the whole sheet up by two: the floor arrow goes to two, zero; the wall arrow to zero, two.

transcript.zh: 把这两个去处竖着写成两列，就是一个矩阵。
transcript.en: Write those two places as two columns, and that's a matrix.

transcript.zh: 变回原样，只往横里拉两倍：地板到二、零，墙还在零、一。
transcript.en: Back to normal, then stretch sideways by two: the floor goes to two, zero; the wall stays at zero, one.

transcript.zh: 再变回来，转九十度：地板转到零、一，墙转到负一、零。
transcript.en: Back again, then turn ninety degrees: the floor turns to zero, one; the wall to minus one, zero.

transcript.zh: 最后像推一摞书那样往右推：地板不动，墙推歪到一、一。
transcript.en: Last, push it to the right like a stack of books: the floor stays put, the wall leans over to one, one.

transcript.zh: 房子推歪了，矩阵记下的，就是两支箭头的去处。
transcript.en: The house leans over, and what the matrix records is where the two arrows went.

transcript.zh: 那第一列二、零，第二列一、一，房子会变成什么样？
transcript.en: So with a first column of two, zero and a second of one, one, what will the house look like?

transcript.zh: 地板箭头到二、零，拉长一倍；墙到一、一，推歪了。
transcript.en: The floor arrow goes to two, zero: twice as long. The wall goes to one, one: pushed over.

transcript.zh: 房子又拉长又推歪，跟两列说的一模一样。
transcript.en: The house is both stretched and pushed over, exactly as the two columns say.

transcript.zh: 按行来读就错了：地板会去二、一，墙去零、一。
transcript.en: Reading by rows is wrong: the floor would go to two, one and the wall to zero, one.

transcript.zh: 房子歪到另一边，跟刚才完全不一样。
transcript.en: The house leans the other way, nothing like before.

transcript.zh: 所以矩阵不是一张死表，它把整个平面一起变形。
transcript.en: So a matrix isn't a dead table: it deforms the whole plane at once.

transcript.zh: 第一列是地板箭头的去处，第二列是墙箭头的去处。
transcript.en: The first column is where the floor arrow goes; the second is where the wall arrow goes.

transcript.zh: 要是两支箭头被压到同一条线上，房子会变成什么？
transcript.en: If the two arrows got squashed onto one line, what would become of the house?

title.en: The Mean Levels the Peaks and Fills the Valleys

aha.zh: 平均数为什么能代表一组数？

misconception.zh: 平均数一定是这组数里出现过的一个数。
misconception.en: The mean has to be one of the numbers in the list.

insight.zh: 把高的削下来、填到矮的上面，总数一块不变，最后大家一样高；这个高度就是平均数，也就是总数除以个数。
insight.en: Shave the tall bars down and fill the short ones up; the total never changes, and everyone ends up the same height. That height is the mean: the total divided by how many there are.

non_example.zh: 来了一个特别大的数，削峰填谷以后平均数被它一个拉高，原来的四个人全都在平均数下面。
non_example.en: Add one very large number, and after levelling the mean is pulled up by it alone; all four original people end up below the mean.

stem.zh: 三个人分别有 2、5、8 颗糖，平均每人几颗？
stem.en: Three people have 2, 5 and 8 sweets. How many is that on average?

stem.zh: 削峰填谷时，为什么最后的高度就是平均数？
stem.en: Why is the final height after levelling the mean?

zh: 总数没变，又平均分给了每一列
因为最高的那列被削掉了
en: The total stays the same and is shared out evenly
Because the tallest bar was cut down
Because we picked the middle number

stem.zh: 5、2、6、3 的平均数是 4，4 在这组数里吗？
stem.en: The mean of 5, 2, 6, 3 is 4. Is 4 in the list?

zh: 不在，平均数不一定是出现过的数
en: No. The mean need not be in the list

stem.zh: 积木图里，「总数」对应什么？
stem.en: In the block picture, what is the total?

en: The height of the tallest bar

stem.zh: 看例子：5、2、6、3 平均数 4。7、3、5 的平均数是多少？
stem.en: Example: 5, 2, 6, 3 has mean 4. What is the mean of 7, 3, 5?

stem.zh: 四次测验平均 80 分，总分是多少？

stem.zh: 4、4、4、4 再加上一个 14，平均数是多少？

stem.zh: 6、9、12 的平均数是多少？

stem.zh: 三个数平均是 7，其中两个是 5 和 6，第三个是多少？

stem.zh: 1、2、3 和 1、2、30，哪组的平均数更能代表大多数人？
stem.en: 1, 2, 3 or 1, 2, 30: whose mean better describes most of the numbers?

transcript.zh: 折纸鹤比赛要报一个“平均每人几只”，这个数代表谁呢？
transcript.en: The paper-crane contest wants one number: cranes per person, on average. Whose number is that?

transcript.zh: 停一下，你心里有答案吗？
transcript.en: Pause here. Do you have an answer?

transcript.zh: 组长觉得，平均数总得和某个人折的一样多吧。

transcript.zh: 我们一起看。四个同学折纸鹤，分别折了五只、两只、六只、三只。
transcript.en: Let's look together. Four classmates folded paper cranes: five, two, six and three.

transcript.zh: 一块积木代表一只纸鹤，高高低低，不一样多。

transcript.zh: 要是平均数是其中一个，就挑三试试，在三块高的地方画一条线。
transcript.en: If the mean were one of them, let's try three and draw a line three blocks high.

transcript.zh: 线上面多出来五块，线下面只缺一块，根本对不上。

transcript.zh: 把高的削下来，填到矮的上面，最后能一样高吗？

transcript.zh: 小林多出的一块，挪给小周。

transcript.zh: 小陈多出的两块，一块给小周，一块给小吴。
transcript.en: Chen's two extra blocks: one to Zhou, one to Wu.

transcript.zh: 四列一样高了，都是四块。
transcript.en: Now all four bars are the same: four blocks each.

transcript.zh: 积木一块没多，一块没少，只是匀了一匀。
transcript.en: Not one block was added or lost. We just evened them out.

transcript.zh: 一共十六块，平均分给四个人，每人正好四块。

transcript.zh: 平均数，就是削峰填谷以后，大家一样高的那个高度。

transcript.zh: 要是又来了一个小郑，一个人就折了九只呢？

transcript.zh: 这时平均数变成五，原来的四个人，全都在线下面。

transcript.zh: 一个特别大的数，一个人就能把平均数拉走。

transcript.zh: 所以平均数，等于总数除以个数。
transcript.en: So the mean is the total divided by how many there are.

title.zh: 抛硬币：频率为什么会稳定
title.en: Coin Flips: Why Frequencies Settle Down

aha.zh: 抛 10 次正面不一定 5 次，那"概率 1/2"说的是什么？

misconception.zh: 连着五次反面，下一次一定该是正面了；抛十次就该是五次正面。
misconception.en: After five tails in a row, the next one has to be heads; ten flips should give exactly five heads.

insight.zh: 概率二分之一不是说十次里一定五次正面，而是说抛得越多，正面出现的频率越会稳定在二分之一附近；前面的乱跳被后面越来越多的次数冲淡，靠的是次数多，不是后面去补前面。
insight.en: A probability of one half doesn't mean exactly five heads in ten flips. It means the more you flip, the more the share of heads settles near one half. The early jumps get diluted by ever more flips; it's the large number that does it, not later flips making up for earlier ones.

non_example.zh: 这一千次里，刚连着出了五个反面的情况有三十一回，下一次是正面的只有十五回，差不多一半：硬币不记得前面出过什么。
non_example.en: In these thousand flips, five tails in a row happened thirty-one times, and the next flip was heads only fifteen of those times, about half: the coin doesn't remember what came before.

stem.zh: 抛一枚均匀硬币 10 次，一定是 5 次正面吗？
stem.en: Flip a fair coin 10 times. Must you get exactly 5 heads?

zh: 不一定，4 次、6 次、7 次都可能
en: Not necessarily: 4, 6 or 7 are all possible

stem.zh: 连着 5 次反面以后，下一次正面的机会是多少？
stem.en: After 5 tails in a row, what is the chance the next flip is heads?

zh: 比一半大，该轮到正面了
比一半小，反面手气正旺
en: More than half: heads is due
Less than half: tails is on a streak

stem.zh: 为什么抛得越多，频率越接近 1/2？
stem.en: Why does the frequency get closer to 1/2 the more you flip?

zh: 后面的抛掷会故意补回前面的
前面的偏差被越来越多的次数冲淡了
en: Later flips deliberately make up for earlier ones
Early lopsidedness gets diluted by more and more flips
The coin gets fairer with use

stem.zh: 看例子：498 次正面 ÷ 1000 次 = 0.498。抛 200 次有 93 次正面，频率是多少？
stem.en: Example: 498 heads ÷ 1000 flips = 0.498. 93 heads in 200 flips: what is the frequency?

stem.zh: 抛 50 次，频率是 0.56，正面有几次？
stem.en: 50 flips with frequency 0.56. How many heads?

stem.zh: 小明抛 10 次得 0.7，小红抛 1000 次得 0.51。谁的结果更接近硬币真正的概率？
stem.en: Ming gets 0.7 from 10 flips; Hong gets 0.51 from 1000 flips. Whose result is closer to the coin's true probability, most likely?

stem.zh: 一个骰子掷了 600 次，掷出 6 的频率大约会是多少？

title.zh: 条件概率：把样本空间缩小
title.en: Conditional Probability: Shrinking the Sample Space

aha.zh: 已知其中一个是男孩，两个都是男孩的概率为什么是 1/3？

misconception.zh: 条件概率等于原来的概率，或者凭感觉说：另一个不是男就是女，所以是二分之一。
misconception.en: A conditional probability equals the plain probability, or by gut feeling: the other child is a boy or a girl, so it's one half.

insight.zh: 条件概率就是把"已知"不可能的情况划掉，在剩下的样本空间里重新数：两个孩子有男男、男女、女男、女女四种一样可能的情况；已知至少一个男孩，划掉女女，剩下三格里两个都是男孩只占一格，所以是三分之一。
insight.en: Conditional probability means crossing out the cases the given information rules out and counting again in what's left. Two children: boy-boy, boy-girl, girl-boy, girl-girl, all equally likely. Given at least one boy, cross out girl-girl; of the three cells left, only one is two boys, so the answer is one third.

non_example.zh: 如果知道的是"老大是男孩"，划掉的是下面一整行，剩下男男、男女两格，这时才是二分之一：条件不同，剩下的样本空间就不同。
non_example.en: If what you know is "the older one is a boy", the whole bottom row is crossed out, leaving boy-boy and boy-girl, and only then is it one half: a different condition leaves a different sample space.

stem.zh: 两个孩子，已知至少一个是男孩，两个都是男孩的概率？
stem.en: Two children, at least one a boy. Chance both are boys?

stem.zh: 为什么分母是 3 而不是 4？
stem.en: Why is the denominator 3 and not 4?

zh: 已知条件划掉了女女，样本空间只剩三格
en: The condition rules out girl-girl, leaving three cells

stem.zh: "至少一个男孩"和"老大是男孩"，为什么答案不一样？
stem.en: Why do "at least one boy" and "the older is a boy" give different answers?

zh: 两个条件划掉的格子不同，剩下的样本空间不同
en: They cross out different cells, so the remaining sample spaces differ
Older children are more likely boys

stem.zh: 看例子：剩下 3 格、阴影 1 格，概率 1/3。掷两颗骰子，已知点数和是 10，两颗都是 5 的概率？

stem.zh: 掷一颗骰子，已知是偶数，是 6 的概率？

stem.zh: 抛两枚硬币，已知至少一枚正面，两枚都是正面的概率？

stem.zh: 已知两个都是男孩，至少一个男孩的概率是多少？和视频里的答案一样吗？
stem.en: Given both are boys, what's the chance of at least one boy? Is it the same as the answer in the video?

zh: 是 1，不一样：条件和结论换位置，概率会变
en: It's 1, not the same: swapping condition and event changes the probability
Same as the answer in the video

next_hook.zh: 已知两个都是男孩，至少一个男孩的概率又是多少？
next_hook.en: Given both are boys, what's the chance of at least one boy?

transcript.zh: 新搬来的邻居家有两个孩子，你只知道，其中至少有一个男孩。
transcript.en: The new neighbours have two children. All you know is that at least one of them is a boy.

transcript.zh: 不用算，凭感觉说：两个都是男孩的可能有多大？

transcript.zh: 朋友脱口而出：二分之一，另一个不是男孩就是女孩嘛。
transcript.en: A friend blurts out: one half, the other one is either a boy or a girl.

transcript.zh: 我们一起看。按老大、老二排，一共四种情况。
transcript.en: Let's look together. Listing older then younger, there are four cases.

transcript.zh: 男男、男女、女男、女女，每一种都一样可能。
transcript.en: Boy-boy, boy-girl, girl-boy, girl-girl: each equally likely.

transcript.zh: 比如男女，是老大男孩、老二女孩；女男正好反过来。
transcript.en: Boy-girl, for example, means older boy, younger girl; girl-boy is the other way round.

transcript.zh: 两个都是男孩只占一格，本来是四分之一。
transcript.en: Two boys is just one cell: one quarter, to begin with.

transcript.zh: 现在多知道了一件事：至少有一个是男孩。
transcript.en: Now we know: at least one is a boy.

transcript.zh: 那么女女这种情况就不可能了，我们把它划掉。
transcript.en: So girl-girl is impossible. Cross it out.

transcript.zh: 样本空间缩小成剩下的三格。
transcript.en: The sample space shrinks to the three cells left.

transcript.zh: 剩下三格里，两个都是男孩的占几格？

transcript.zh: 只有一格，所以概率是三分之一，不是二分之一。
transcript.en: Just one, so the probability is one third, not one half.

transcript.zh: 剩下的三格机会相同，阴影占一格，就是一除以三。
transcript.en: The three remaining cells are still equally likely, and the shaded one is one of them: one divided by three.

transcript.zh: 说二分之一的人，其实是把男女和女男当成了同一种情况。
transcript.en: Saying one half treats boy-girl and girl-boy as a single case.

transcript.zh: 换一个条件：这回知道的是，老大是男孩。

transcript.zh: 这次划掉的是下面一整行，剩下男男、男女两格。
transcript.en: This time the whole bottom row is crossed out, leaving boy-boy and boy-girl.

transcript.zh: 这时才是二分之一。条件一变，剩下的样本空间就变了。
transcript.en: Only now is it one half. Change the condition, and what's left changes.

transcript.zh: 所以条件概率，就是先划掉不可能的，再在剩下的里面数。
transcript.en: So conditional probability means crossing out what's impossible, then counting in what's left.

transcript.zh: 分母不再是全部四格，而是划完以后剩下的三格。
transcript.en: The denominator is no longer all four cells, just the three that remain.

transcript.zh: 已知两个都是男孩，至少一个男孩的概率又是多少？
transcript.en: Given both are boys, what's the chance of at least one boy?

title.en: The Galton Board and the Binomial Distribution

aha.zh: 为什么小球会堆成"钟形"？

misconception.zh: 每个格子落球的机会一样，球该落得差不多平。
misconception.en: Every slot is equally likely, so the balls should land roughly flat.

insight.zh: 每个球在每颗钉子上往左往右各一半，所以每一条路的机会都一样；落进哪一格只看往右拐了几次，通向中间格子的路最多（一、六、十五、二十、十五、六、一），所以球堆成中间高两边低的钟形。
insight.en: At every peg a ball goes left or right with equal chance, so every route is equally likely. Which slot it lands in depends only on how many rights it took, and the middle slots have the most routes (1, 6, 15, 20, 15, 6, 1), so the balls pile into a bell shape.

non_example.zh: 如果七格机会一样，一百二十八个球每格该有十八个左右；实际最边上只落了三个和两个，中间一格有三十九个。
non_example.en: If the seven slots were equally likely, 128 balls would give about eighteen each; in fact the outer slots got three and two, and the middle got thirty-nine.

stem.zh: 高尔顿板有 6 层钉子、7 个格子。球最可能落在哪？
stem.en: A Galton board has 6 rows of pegs and 7 slots. Where is a ball most likely to land?

stem.zh: 为什么中间的格子球最多？
stem.en: Why does the middle slot get the most balls?

zh: 通向中间的路最多，而每条路机会一样
en: More routes lead there, and every route is equally likely

stem.zh: 4 层钉子时，5 个格子的路数是多少？
stem.en: With 4 rows of pegs, how many routes lead to each of the 5 slots?

stem.zh: 看例子：128 个球，中间一格约 128×20÷64 = 40 个。左数第二格约多少个？
stem.en: Example: with 128 balls the middle slot gets about 128×20÷64 = 40. About how many in the second slot from the left?

stem.zh: 6 层钉子，球落进最左边一格的概率是多少？
stem.en: 6 rows of pegs: what is the chance a ball lands in the leftmost slot?

stem.zh: 抛 4 次硬币，正好 2 次正面的概率是多少？
stem.en: Flip a coin 4 times. What is the chance of exactly 2 heads?

stem.zh: 抛 6 次硬币：正好 3 次正面和 6 次全是正面，哪个更可能？
stem.en: Flip 6 coins: exactly 3 heads, or all 6 heads — which is more likely?

next_hook.zh: 抛十次硬币正好五次正面，又该怎么数路呢？
next_hook.en: Ten coin flips with exactly five heads: how would you count the routes for that?

transcript.zh: 游园会上有个弹珠游戏：小球一路碰着钉子，掉进七个格子。
transcript.en: At the school fair there's a marble game: a ball bounces off pins all the way down and lands in one of seven slots.

transcript.zh: 倒下一大把球，你猜它们会落成什么样子？
transcript.en: Pour in a whole handful of balls. What shape do you think they will land in?

transcript.zh: 摊主说：七个格子机会一样，球该落得差不多平。
transcript.en: The stall keeper says: all seven slots are equally likely, so the balls should land about flat.

transcript.zh: 我们一起看。球每碰到一颗钉子，就往左或往右，机会各一半。
transcript.en: Let's look together. Each time a ball hits a peg, it goes left or right, half and half.

transcript.zh: 一共六层钉子，落进哪一格，只看它往右拐了几次。
transcript.en: There are six rows of pegs; the slot it lands in depends only on how many times it went right.

transcript.zh: 这个球是左右左左左右，往右两次，落进左数第三格。
transcript.en: This ball went left, right, left, left, left, right: two rights, so it lands in the third slot from the left.

transcript.zh: 再落九个，一共十个，各格高高低低，看不出规律。
transcript.en: Drop nine more, ten in all: the slots are up and down, with no pattern yet.

transcript.zh: 落一百多个球以后，七个格子会一样高吗？
transcript.en: After more than a hundred balls, will the seven slots be the same height?

transcript.zh: 再落一百一十八个，一共一百二十八个。
transcript.en: Drop a hundred and eighteen more: a hundred and twenty-eight in all.

transcript.zh: 中间高、两边低，堆成了一座山。
transcript.en: High in the middle, low at the sides: they've piled into a hill.

transcript.zh: 最边上两格只有三个和两个，正中间有三十九个。
transcript.en: The two outer slots have only three and two; the middle one has thirty-nine.

transcript.zh: 为什么？因为通向中间的路多。
transcript.en: Why? Because there are more routes to the middle.

transcript.zh: 落进最左边，六次都得往左，只有一条路。
transcript.en: To land at the far left, all six turns must be left: just one route.

transcript.zh: 落进正中间，三左三右，顺序随便排，有二十条路。
transcript.en: To land in the middle: three lefts and three rights in any order, twenty routes.

transcript.zh: 七个格子的路数是一、六、十五、二十、十五、六、一。
transcript.en: The routes to the seven slots number one, six, fifteen, twenty, fifteen, six, one.

transcript.zh: 一共六十四条，每条路的机会一样，路多的格子球就多。
transcript.en: Sixty-four in all, each route equally likely, so slots with more routes get more balls.

transcript.zh: 按路数算，中间一格该有四十个左右，实际三十九个。
transcript.en: By the route count, the middle should get about forty; in fact it got thirty-nine.

transcript.zh: 要是七格机会一样，每格该有十八个左右，两边远远不到。
transcript.en: If the seven slots were equally likely, each would hold about eighteen. The sides are nowhere near.

transcript.zh: 所以钟形是数出来的：通向中间的路最多。
transcript.en: So the bell shape comes from counting: the most routes lead to the middle.

transcript.zh: 这是演示，不是证明；这些路数就是二项分布的来历。
transcript.en: This is a demonstration, not a proof; these route counts are where the binomial distribution comes from.

transcript.zh: 抛十次硬币正好五次正面，又该怎么数路呢？
transcript.en: Ten coin flips with exactly five heads: how would you count the routes for that?

title.en: Finite Differences: The Discrete Derivative

aha.zh: 为什么 n² 的"差的差"是常数？

misconception.zh: 数列和函数是两回事；差的差是常数这种题只能背题型。
misconception.en: Sequences and functions are different worlds; 'the second difference is constant' is just a problem type to memorise.

insight.zh: 一辆车第 n 秒停在 n 平方的位置，路标是 0、1、4、9、16、25：每秒走的路是相邻路标的距离 1、3、5、7、9，像速度；这些距离每秒多 2，像加速度。路标越来越稀、却稀得很均匀，这个均匀就是二阶差分是常数，正对应导数 2x 和 2。
insight.en: A car stops at n squared after n seconds, so the signposts are 0, 1, 4, 9, 16, 25. Each second it covers the gap between neighbouring posts, 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, like a speed; those gaps grow by 2 each second, like an acceleration. The posts spread out, but evenly: that evenness is the constant second difference, matching the derivatives 2x and 2.

non_example.zh: 二的 n 次方 1、2、4、8、16，每秒走的路还是 1、2、4、8，越拉越开，怎么差都不会变成常数。
non_example.en: Powers of two, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16: the gaps are 1, 2, 4, 8 again, spreading faster and faster, never constant however many times you take differences.

stem.zh: 1、4、9、16、25 相邻两项的差是多少？
stem.en: What are the gaps between 1, 4, 9, 16, 25?

stem.zh: 边长 n 的正方形变成 n+1，为什么多出 2n+1 格？
stem.en: Why does a square grow by 2n+1 cells when its side goes from n to n+1?

zh: 两条 n 格的长条加一个角块
en: Two strips of n plus one corner
Each of four sides gains one cell

stem.zh: 差分 2n+1 比导数 2x 多出来的 1 是什么？
stem.en: What is the extra 1 in the difference 2n+1 compared with the derivative 2x?

en: The corner: with dx = 1 it can't be dropped
A constant added for no reason

stem.en: Example: 0, 1, 4, 9, 16 has first differences 1, 3, 5, 7 and second difference 2. What is the second difference of 2, 5, 10, 17, 26?

stem.zh: 数列 3、7、13、21、31 的下一项是多少？
stem.en: What comes next in 3, 7, 13, 21, 31?

stem.zh: 立方数 0、1、8、27、64、125 要差几次才变成常数？
stem.en: How many rounds of differences make the cubes 0, 1, 8, 27, 64, 125 constant?

next_hook.zh: 那立方数，要差几次才变成常数？
next_hook.en: Next: how many rounds of differences does it take for the cubes to become constant?

transcript.zh: 练习册上有道找规律题，开头是零、一、四、九、十六。
transcript.en: A workbook has a find-the-pattern puzzle that starts zero, one, four, nine, sixteen.

transcript.zh: 相邻的差再求一次差，全是二。这是巧合吗？
transcript.en: Take the gaps, then the gaps between those: all twos. Is that a coincidence?

transcript.zh: 前桌摆摆手：这是数列题，跟函数不沾边，背题型就行。
transcript.en: The kid in front waves it off: it's a sequence problem, nothing to do with functions, just memorise the type.

transcript.zh: 上一集边长多长了一小段 d x；现在把边长换成时间。
transcript.en: Last time the side grew by a little dx. Now let's swap the side for time.

transcript.zh: 一辆车第 n 秒停在 n 平方的位置，停在哪，就在哪插一根路标。
transcript.en: A car stops at n squared after n seconds, and we plant a signpost wherever it stops.

transcript.zh: 第一秒停在一，第二秒到四，然后九、十六、二十五。
transcript.en: After one second it's at one, after two at four, then nine, sixteen, twenty-five.

transcript.zh: 路标越来越稀，可是稀得很均匀。
transcript.en: The signposts spread further apart, but they spread out evenly.

transcript.zh: 每秒走的路，一秒比一秒多多少？
transcript.en: How much further does the car go each second than the second before?

transcript.zh: 每秒走的路，就是相邻路标的距离：一、三、五、七、九。
transcript.en: The distance each second is the gap between neighbouring posts: one, three, five, seven, nine.

transcript.zh: 这些距离一秒比一秒多二：二、二、二、二。
transcript.en: Each of those is two more than the one before: two, two, two, two.

transcript.zh: 路标稀得均匀，就是这个多出来的二一直不变。
transcript.en: The posts spread out evenly because that extra two never changes.

transcript.zh: 每秒走的路像速度，它就是差分二 n 加一，对上导数二 x。
transcript.en: Distance per second is like a speed: the difference two n plus one, matching the derivative two x.

transcript.zh: 每秒多走的像加速度，是二阶差分二，对上二 x 的导数二。
transcript.en: Extra distance per second is like an acceleration: the second difference two, matching the derivative of two x, which is two.

transcript.zh: 多出来的那个一，就是上一集丢不掉的角块。
transcript.en: The extra one is the corner we couldn't drop last time.

transcript.zh: 换成二的 n 次方：一、二、四、八、十六。
transcript.en: Now try powers of two: one, two, four, eight, sixteen.

transcript.zh: 每秒走的还是一、二、四、八，越拉越开，永远不均匀。
transcript.en: The gaps are one, two, four, eight again: they spread faster and faster, never evenly.

transcript.zh: 所以平方数的二阶差分是常数，正像 x 平方的二阶导数是常数。
transcript.en: So the second difference of the squares is constant, just as the second derivative of x squared is constant.

transcript.zh: 数列的差分和函数的导数，是同一件事的两个版本。
transcript.en: Differences of a sequence and derivatives of a function are two versions of the same idea.

transcript.zh: 还记得等差数列的台阶吗？一加三加五加七加九，正好拼成五乘五。
transcript.en: Remember the staircases of arithmetic series? One plus three plus five plus seven plus nine makes exactly five by five.

transcript.zh: 一圈一圈加上去的，正是差分算出来的那些数。
